items.title: Excessive or reasonable? Police actions at Sydney's protest analysed
items.description: What is reasonable? It's a question being asked by some after footage of clashes in Sydney's CBD, during a rally against Israeli President Isaac Herzog's visit.

items.title: Israel undermines two-state solution while Herzog visits Australia
items.description: While Israeli President Isaac Herzog visited Sydney, his government was taking concrete actions in the West Bank designed to "continue to kill the idea of a Palestinian state".

items.title: As Epstein spotlight shifts to UK, Trump could have 3 million reasons to worry
items.description: Donald Trump's enemies made no secret of their hopes the documents would contain something explosive enough to bring the president down, but right now the Epstein spotlight is on Britain's politicians and palaces.

items.title: Woman 'frustrated and mystified' after Uber guide dog case settles
items.description: Uber quietly agrees to an external review of its Australian operations after settling a Federal Court case brought by a woman refused more than 30 rides while travelling with a guide dog.

items.title: Liberals plot mass resignations paving way for leadership challenge
items.description: Liberals are bracing for a wave of frontbench resignations as soon as Wednesday to pave the way for Angus Taylor to mount a leadership challenge against Sussan Ley.

items.title: Live: Cam Bolton fractures neck as training falls rule two Aussies out of Games
items.description: Australia's Cam Bolton and Misaki Vaughan are ruled out of the Games after training falls, while reigning Olympic gold medallist Jakara Anthony advances to the women's moguls final at the Milano Cortina Games. Follow live.

items.title: What is a 'capacity constraint' and why should you care?
items.description: It may sound boring, but "capacity constraints" are to blame for your higher mortgage repayments.

items.title: A month on from Iran's protests, reports emerge of security forces 'refusing orders'
items.description: As talks between Washington and Tehran over a nuclear deal continue, fractures within the regime are starting to emerge.

items.title: FBI releases doorbell camera photos from Nancy Guthrie's home
items.description: FBI director Kash Patel has posted the images on social media, saying they had been recovered after days of work by investigators.

items.title: Live: Commonwealth Bank profit beats expectations, rising to $5.4b
items.description: The Australian share market is likely to rise ahead of the first big day of reporting season. Some of the nation's largest companies, such as Commonwealth Bank, CSL and AGL Energy, are reporting. Follow live.

items.title: Major change could be coming to supermarket shelves
items.description: The nation's food ministers will this week take a crucial step towards mandating the Health Star Rating scheme on packaged food products.

items.title: Sharks had never been seen this far south. Then one swam into view
items.description: A slow-moving sleeper shark captured on camera deep below the ocean surface near the South Shetland Islands is the first shark species to ever be found in Antarctic waters.

items.title: ASIO ordered independent review into Bondi terror case, stands by 2019 assessment
items.description: The nation's top spy has welcomed a royal commission into the Bondi terror attack, vowing to "own any mistakes" uncovered by the probe as his agency comes under pressure over whether the tragedy could have been prevented.

items.title: Images of alleged tobacco wars kingpin released as police vow to crush syndicate
items.description: Hamad was deported from Australia in 2023 and has been a key person of interest relating to firebombings at Victorian tobacco shops and businesses.

items.title: Rental affordability hits record low in Australia
items.description: Tenants now pay an average of 33.4 per cent of their pre-tax income on rent, which is the highest level on record, according to a property research firm.

items.title: Marsh backs unrecognisable Aussie team ahead of T20 World Cup opener
items.description: Despite a slew of key injuries leaving the Australian team unrecognisable, captain Mitch Marsh is confident about the experience left in the side.

items.title: Practical ways to avoid feeling lonely or isolated while working from home
items.description: Working remotely can be a lonely experience. Here's what you can do about it.

items.title: E-bike seller uses fake compliance stickers to skirt crackdown
items.description: An e-bike seller agrees to help a buyer avoid police detection by putting fake compliance stickers on high-powered bikes to make them look road legal.

items.title: Largest quarterly bulk-billing increase outside of COVID recorded
items.description: Bulk-billing rates have rebounded in the first clear measure of the impact of the government's multi-billion-dollar pledge.

items.title: SA Liberals face wipeout not seen since state bank election
items.description: Labor faced a humiliating election loss following the state bank collapse in the early 90s. Now, recent polling shows a collapse of another kind could be brewing for the Liberal Party with One Nation hot on its heels.

items.title: Maps reveal where more high-rise apartments could be built in Melbourne
items.description: The state government releases draft maps of the remaining activity centres around Melbourne that show apartments of up to 20 storeys could be built in the south-east.

items.title: Hospital staff shortage in spotlight after former administrator's fall
items.description: David Walshaw spent 20 years looking after the Limestone Coast's hospitals, but a fall made him realise the system was failing patients.

items.title: Surgeon Kelvin Kong's life growing up Chinese and Indigenous in Australia
items.description: Australia's first identified First Nations surgeon, Dr Kelvin Kong spoke about his Malaysian Chinese heritage during the annual Wang Gungwu lecture at Parliament House.

items.title: Developers desert plans for new apartments in Western Sydney
items.description: Industry peak bodies and economists blame mounting construction costs and rising interest rates for the stalling of new apartment projects in Western Sydney.

items.title: Nearly 15,000 tyres are dumped in Melbourne's north every year and one council wants action
items.description: A council in Melbourne's north wants the federal government to establish a free tyre recycling scheme to stop thousands of tyres being dumped, causing a potential environmental hazard.
